question.problem:
The table below gives the values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p,$ where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. Find the value of $z$ such that $P(Z>z)=0.10.$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $p$ | $\,0.900\,$ | $\,0.950\,$ | $\,0.975\,$ | $\,0.990\,$ | $\,0.995\,$ | $\,0.999\,$ | $\,0.9995\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.9600\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ | $\,2.5758\,$ | $\,3.0902\,$ | $\,3.2905\,$ |

$z=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we express the given information in terms of $Φ,$ using the complement:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z>z) & =0.10 \\ 1-P(Z\le z) & =0.10 \\ 1-Φ(z) & =0.10 \\ Φ(z) & =1-0.10 \\ Φ(z) & =0.90\end{aligned}
$$

So, we are looking for the value of $z$ such that

$$
z={Φ}^{-1}(0.90).
$$

We look for the column in the table that corresponds to $p=0.90,$ and we find that

$$
p=0.90\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(p)=1.2816.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
z={Φ}^{-1}(0.90)=1.2816.
$$
